'''Marina Logares Jiménez''' (born 1976, in [[Madrid]]) is a Spanish mathematician and LGBT+ activist. She was named one of the 50 most influential LGBT+ people in Spain in 2019.

== Career ==
Logares was awarded her PhD in mathematics in 2006 from the [[Autonomous University of Madrid]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|url=http://www.agenciasinc.es/Entrevistas/La-ciencia-inclusiva-no-se-hace-sola-hay-que-trabajarsela|title=La ciencia inclusiva no se hace sola, hay que trabajársela|last=Científicas|first=SINC Servicio de Información y Noticias|date=2019-06-29|website=www.agenciasinc.es|language=es|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucm.es/marina_logares/curriculum|title=Marina Logares Jiménez|website=www.ucm.es|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref> She later worked at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics|Max Planck Institute]] in Bonn, the [[University of Oxford]], the [[University of Porto]] and the [[University of Plymouth]].<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7">{{Cite news|url=https://elpais.com/elpais/2019/05/28/ciencia/1559071397_626794.html|title=Las lesbianas somos invisibles|last=Ansede|first=Manuel|date=2019-05-29|work=El País|access-date=2020-01-11|language=es|issn=1134-6582}}</ref> She is currently a visiting professor at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]].<ref name=":6" /> Logares studies within the field of geometry. Her areas of interest in research focus on algebraic and complex geometry and mathematical physics. She particularly studies [[Yang–Mills equations]], and their derivatives, Hitchin equations.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.icmat.es/es/mlogares|title=Marina Logares {{!}}|website=www.icmat.es|access-date=2020-01-11|archive-date=2019-07-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190705155901/https://www.icmat.es/es/mlogares|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2018 she published the book ''Las geometrías y otras revoluciones'' (Geometry and other revolutions),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elperiodicodeaqui.com/epda-noticias/la-matematica-marina-logares-publica--las-geometrias-y-otras-revoluciones-/169036|title=La matemática Marina Logares publica|website=El Periódico de Aquí|language=es|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref> which describes the history of the field of geometry.<ref name=":7" />

== Activism ==
Logares is notable for her social engagement, particularly her participation in the struggle for the LGBT community's rights and inclusion in science. She is a [[lesbian]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=brilla |first=Gente que |date=2019-07-31 |title=Marina Logares, matemática y activista por los derechos LGTBI |url=https://gentequebrilla.es/2019/07/31/marina-logares-matematica-y-activista-por-los-derechos-lgtbi/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230921233022/https://gentequebrilla.es/2019/07/31/marina-logares-matematica-y-activista-por-los-derechos-lgtbi/ |archive-date=September 21, 2023 |access-date=2020-01-11 |website=Gente que brilla |language=es}}</ref><ref name=":7" /> At the university of Plymouth, Logares was the co-chair of the LGBT co-forum.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=http://blog.math-sciences.org/academic-in-top-50-most-influential-lgbt-people|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111182156/http://blog.math-sciences.org/academic-in-top-50-most-influential-lgbt-people|url-status=usurped|archive-date=January 11, 2020|title=Academic in top 50 most influential LGBT people – Blog for Mathematical Sciences at Plymouth University|language=en-US|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref> In 2019 she was included in a list of the 50 most influential LGBT people in Spain by newspaper ''[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]''.<ref name=":8" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elmundo.es/album/loc/famosos/2019/06/22/5d0b70affc6c8354068b4652_50.html|title=Marina Logares|date=2019-06-21|website=ELMUNDO|language=es|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref> In 2020 she was the keynote speaker the LGBT STEMinar in Birmingham, UK.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://lgbtstem.wordpress.com/lgbt-steminar-2020/|title=LGBTQ+ STEMinar 2020|date=2019-04-14|website=LGBTQ+ STEM|language=en|access-date=2020-01-11}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Logares is a 3rd degree black belt in [[Taekwondo]]<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":7" /> and black belt in [[Hapkido]].

== Articles ==
Some of her publications are:
* Paper 'Moduli Spaces of Framed G–Higgs Bundles and Symplectic Geometry'. With Indranil Biswas and Ana Peón Nieto. July 2019.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Marina_Logares|title=Marina Logares {{!}} PhD Mathematics {{!}} University of Plymouth, Plymouth {{!}} UoP {{!}} School of Computing Electronics and Mathematics|access-date=13 September 2019|website=ResearchGate|language=en}}</ref>
* Paper 'On Higgs Bundles on Nodal Curves'. March 2019.<ref name=":4" />
* Book 'Las matemáticas y otras revoluciones'. Colección ¿Qué sabemos de? del CSIC y Catarata, 2018.<ref>{{cite book|title=Las geometrías y otras revoluciones|editor=CSIC|date=2018|isbn=9788490975558|oclc=1082518053|last=Logares|first=Marina}}</ref>
* Paper 'A lax monoidal Topological Quantum Field Theory for representation varieties'. With Ángel González-Prieto. September 2017.<ref name=":4" />
* Paper 'Bohr--Sommerfeld Lagrangians of moduli spaces of Higgs bundles'. With Indranil Biswas and Niels Leth Gammelgaard. September 2014.<ref name=":4" />
* Hodge-Deligne polynomials of SL(2,C)-character varieties for curves of small genus'. With Vicente Muñoz y Peter E. Newstead. June 2011.<ref name=":4" />
* Artículo 'A Torelli theorem for the moduli space of parabolic Higgs bundles'. Con Tomás L. Gómez. Mayo 2009.<ref name=":4" />
* Thesis 'Parabolic U(p;q)Higgs bundles'. May 2006.<ref name=":4" />
